searchText: I'm creatinga very nice utility function for deposits and participating in testnets If all client teams could send me their preferred key format for loading into a validator that would be aswesome and if you dont have a key format! Prysmatic uses a .json with the following format: ``` { "keys": [{ "validator_key": "base64encoded BLS secret key", }, { "validator_key": "base64encoded BLS secret key", }] } ``` This works well, it lets you load as many keys into a validator. But if you have another methods just let me know the format and I'll add support for it Prysm format is pretty good And it is simple, all key files in one folder Small caveat, the above format is solely for testing as it makes reading keys much faster . For normal validators we are using the web3 secret storage format. https://github.com/ethereum/wiki/wiki/Web3-Secret-Storage-Definition We will be looking to update it to the new keystore standard soon And if you want to try out the new keystore and associated standards you can use ethdo https://github.com/wealdtech/ethdo to create wallets and keys. Having validators able to read this format would allow for interoperability between validator implementations <@!476250636548308992> waaait so are you saying i can or cannot boot up my validators with that format? It'll work in the testnet right? <@!144468805697929216> briefly reading it doesn't really have support for multiple keys In what way does it not? Each account is named in the format 'wallet/address', so you can create as many keys as you like in whichever wallets you like. (and prysm testnet will work with that unencrypted key format for now, I'd imagine it'll stay around for a while at least) <@322222239850168331> oh it will work fine :) , just that it is only ever used for testing by us. So you can spin up multiple validators quickly with it. Just that you shouldnt ever run it with actual money behind it We're migrating over to EIP-2335 for production. Presently we store a file for each validator that contains the ssz bytes for: ```rust Keypair { secret, public } ``` <@!476250636548308992> oh lol ya <@!361447803194441738> cool thats what we use - Is there a fast way of attaching batch amount of keys? Or do i need to manually do something like `--key address,address,..,...` We have a `~/.lighthouse/validators` that has a directory for each validator (named their public key). When the VC boots it'll just open all validators in that directory. dope `lighthouse account validator new random 1337` will make 1337 random keys in that directory so something like ``` validators ├── v1 │ └── key └── v2 └── key ``` `lighthouse account validator new insecure 0 1337` will create those "deterministic" keypairs that are just based upon their validator index. That command will create all validator for the range `0..1337`. mm im going to be creating my own keypairs because i want to recover the 1m Goerli eth lol ``` validators ├── 0xa070ce5b65a96afb5e4315e8fa118a0e0eca472197f23634736851b9d7d3334874392098389889e1607ad9bc3ae194e8 │ ├── eth1_deposit_data.rlp │ ├── voting_keypair │ └── withdrawal_keypair └── 0xaae1fbec9ba9798b75908f7bff7c66c2a8041be2eaba44272f349038dbcfcca16f527be1d407e3917fdd5696120c75ef ├── eth1_deposit_data.rlp ├── voting_keypair └── withdrawal_keypair ``` oh interesting if i don't supply the deposit data will it bug out? I'll be doing the deposits myself Nope, the val client doesn't care about the deposit data. Feel free to omit 🙂 kk I'll have that support shortly merci not sure if it's too much extra work, but being able to convert from one format to the other is also valuable im generating the prysmatic json from the eip standard should be trivial we can add the eip standard. AFAIK, <@!144468805697929216> already wrote a library that supports it tbh tho- for testing the json file is really nice cool, if you've some sort of hub model, where everything can be converted to the standard, then we can convert between the other formats too. 10/10 design decision as long as yu don't commit the keys what format are the other chains using? ie since bls is getting standardised, I'd expect they'll come up with some serialization format as well? we're doing something similar to lighthouse, just dumping a bunch of files with keys in them in a folder and reading from there <@!203220829473996800> pls don't do key conversion. pls use same format. the reason is not extra work, the reason is running multi-client and avoid slashing. same format of key store is one helpful factor to avoid slashing. pls read my slashing prevention suggestion on prysm github {{4640}} https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/issues/4640 <@!322222239850168331> <@!361447803194441738> I think we're talking about two different things I agree that ideally we have one standard format. That said, I am not sure how quick clients are to adopt something like that, so a basic conversion as temporary solution helps I'm trying to effectively "hack" lol but mass scale testing this format makes it really convenient for me (the prysm json format) There are standards for most bits that are at least proposed; file locations and names are still pending but I've written an EIP for that just haven't published them. But yeah, will take a while for people to converge on something

excerpts.author: paulhauner
excerpts.content:
We're migrating over to EIP-2335 for production. Presently we store a file for each validator that contains the ssz bytes for:

```rust
Keypair {
  secret,
  public
}
```
